title: Florida's 23rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Florida's 23rd Congressional District, redrawn in 2026 to cover coastal Palm Beach County from West Palm Beach to Delray Beach, is rated Solid Democratic with a D+9 partisan lean. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Lois Frankel, who previously represented the 22nd District, shifted her candidacy to the new 23rd District and faces two Democratic primary challengers: attorney Victoria Doyle and Mark Piper. Two Republicans, Deborah Adeimy and Paola Branda, are also running. The August 18 primary will determine the nominees for the November 3 general election in this heavily Democratic district where Kamala Harris won over 56% of the vote in 2024.

candidates.name: Lois Frankel
candidates.summary: Lois Frankel has served as U.S. Representative for Florida's 22nd Congressional District since 2013 and shifted her candidacy to the new 23rd District after redistricting. She previously served as Mayor of West Palm Beach (2003-2011) and in the Florida House of Representatives (1986-1992, 1994-2002), including as Minority Leader. Frankel holds a B.A. from Boston University and a J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center.

candidates.name: Victoria Doyle
candidates.summary: Victoria Doyle is a Lake Worth Beach attorney and local activist running in the Democratic primary against incumbent Lois Frankel. She is a trademark attorney who has filed a lawsuit challenging the renaming of Palm Beach International Airport after Donald Trump. Doyle emphasizes ending the status quo and has positioned herself as a progressive alternative to Frankel.

forecast.rationale: This forecast is based on district fundamentals and candidate context, as no public polling exists in the race data. Florida's 23rd CD is rated Solid Democratic with a D+9 partisan lean, and Kamala Harris won over 56% of the vote here in 2024, establishing a strong Democratic baseline. Incumbent Rep. Lois Frankel shifted from the old 22nd District into this new coastal Palm Beach County district centered on her political base of West Palm Beach. She is an established officeholder (serving since 2013, former Mayor of West Palm Beach, former state House Minority Leader) with high name recognition and institutional advantages. While she faces two Democratic primary challengers (Victoria Doyle and Mark Piper), incumbency and fundraising advantages make her the clear favorite to win the August 18 primary. The Republican field (Deborah Adeimy and Paola Branda) shows no signs of unusual strength. The D+9 lean and safe_d rating indicate Democrats are overwhelming favorites in the general election regardless of nominee. Confidence is medium rather than high due to the absence of polling and the fact that redistricting (the district was redrawn in 2026) slightly elevates uncertainty, though the fundamental partisan environment heavily favors the Democratic candidate.
